children: Lenovo Group is scheduled to report fiscal second-quarter results on Thursday. Here is what you need to know:

NET PROFIT: The world's largest maker of personal computers is expected to post adjusted net profit of $1.27 billion for the three months ended September, according to a Visible Alpha poll, more than doubling from a year earlier. Its reported net profit likely came in at $90,000, weighed by a noncash fair-value loss related to its ALAT warrant.
REVENUE: Revenue likely rose 36% to $27.80 billion, supported by growth in its infrastructure-solutions business on surging demand for AI servers.

Lenovo's shares have swung wildly in recent quarters. The stock has wiped out the 50% advance it made in the three months ended September, trimming its gains for the year to nearly 80%. Investors initially cheered the company's goal of hitting the $100 billion revenue mark this fiscal year, ahead of its original schedule, thanks to robust AI infrastructure demand. However, mounting doubts about the sustainability of the AI trade have damped sentiment lately.

Global PC shipments fell 20% in the July-September period, according to industry tracker IDC. Continued supply constraints and the inventory pull-in earlier in the year, as vendors and channels rushed to stock up ahead of memory-chip-driven price hikes, left the quarter with little demand to draw on. Lenovo remained the world's largest PC maker by shipments during the quarter, with a 23.8% market share.

Lenovo's AI infrastructure momentum should be intact despite recent market volatility, analysts said. While there have been increasing market concerns surrounding highly leveraged AI infrastructure operators such as CoreWeave, a client of Lenovo, the company's direct exposure to higher-risk neocloud customers remains limited, Citi analysts noted. Still, investors will pay attention to management comments on future AI demand, especially after the Democratic sweep in U.S. midterm elections is expected to intensify regulatory scrutiny and slow the data-center buildout.
